what_went_well: Tests and docs complete; it flagged the 74-versus-actual characters drift in my brief.
waste: 10 reads of extract60.py (about 3,000 lines), 14 reads before the first edit. Thinking about 40% of output (estimate). Rejected on review, so all 78 calls were redone in the next job.
claude_would_have_done: Measured where thin pages sit (one query) before writing any code. That query showed all 352 inside multi-page chunks, which the worker's design missed.
claude_estimate: About 25 calls for the code, at far higher token cost per call than the worker.
prompt_change: State the measured data shape in the brief and require a measurement against real data before design. Name exact functions and line ranges for large files.
scope_change: The brief also asked for the number-override rule before anyone had measured it; take untested rules out of scope.

what_went_well: Fastest job of the day, 6 minutes, with a verbatim defect list and required behaviours; self-report within 1 call of actual; it found and fixed the selection path.
waste: 21 calls before first edit against 12, re-reading the same overlay code the previous job had just read. Thinking about 49% of output (estimate), the highest of the four.
claude_would_have_done: Same design; I would have started from the diff instead of the module, so about 8 reads.
prompt_change: Keep this format: defect, evidence, required behaviour, fixtures. Give the function names to start from, because the reader had none.
scope_change: Right size. A worker fixing a branch should get that branch's diff in the brief.

what_went_well: The contract gate works: 108 failing rows stayed out, including two false NIM values. The loader refuses unmapped measures. Exact quotes hold, 0 failures in 33.
waste: 164 calls against 90, 30 before first edit by the status record, while its report says 58 before first edit and about 155 total, both wrong. 9 reads of execute.py, 27 greps. Two defects still needed fixing on review: a filing date used as a period, and three-letter terms dropped.
claude_would_have_done: Split it into three jobs: fact loader, passage search, KEC loader. KEC's loader alone is about 15 calls. I would have kept the period rule strict from the start.
claude_estimate: About 60 calls across the three parts.
prompt_change: Say what a missing field must do: a required field with no value is refused and counted, never filled from another field.
permission_change: None. Leaving the real database write to me after review worked.
scope_change: One deliverable per worker. Three in one brief gave the worst overrun of the day.

job_type: code: pipeline change plus new command
what_went_well: Found one existing matcher to reuse, as asked; fixtures match the brief; flagged that repair drops resolutions.
waste: 95 calls against 70, reported about 84. 27 before first edit against 15, 17 of them reads; 9 reads of extract60.py. It took the first number within 2% instead of the closest, found on review.
claude_would_have_done: Same design, and I would have split the write-time check from the re-read command.
prompt_change: When reusing a tolerance match to identify something, say to take the closest. Give file and function pointers: _write, validate, printed tokens.
scope_change: Four parts; the re-read command could have been its own job.

job_type: Claude session: orchestration and review, 2 Nov
what_went_well: Review caught four defects before merge, the biggest being the OCR overlay that would have skipped every thin page.
waste: I wrote code myself: thin_pages, hp_ocr_pages, kec_fetch changes and merge fixes, against the reviewer role. My wait ended at T-038 and I started no new one, so a crashed HP job sat idle for 12 minutes and I reported it as running without checking. Two commits blocked by the docs gate.
claude_would_have_done: Not applicable: this row is my own work. Small one-file helpers were faster by hand, but they still count against the rule and should be logged as such.
prompt_change: Set budgets from the measured median in this log, not by guess: all four jobs exceeded both limits, so a budget nobody meets teaches nothing.
scope_change: Rearm a wait covering every running job whenever any one finishes, and check live status before reporting state.

job_type: code: new report script plus gate logging
what_went_well: Gate results unchanged and proved by test; a rule nothing measures says not measured; its real report already shows direct code commits as sidelined.
waste: 83 calls against 70, reported 81; 28 before first edit against 15. It lost time on a sandbox temp-folder permission fault. It also wrongly reported that test_hp_headless does not exist: the file is there and 10 tests pass.
claude_would_have_done: Checked the test folder by name before calling it drift. Left out the Workers sheet, which overlaps T-043.
prompt_change: Say that tests must not use the sandbox pytest temp folder, and warn about the known ACL fault up front. Ask for evidence for any claim of repo drift.
permission_change: None. The change to the start gate in core.py needs a server restart to take effect, so briefs should say so.
scope_change: Two workers started on overlapping log sheets because I opened T-043 after T-042 began. Check running briefs for overlap before starting another.

what_went_well: Self-report within 1 of actual (72 against 71), the most accurate of the day. Left host and tickets blank rather than guess. Its own check caught that first edit must count write as well as edit.
waste: 71 calls against 55, 22 before first edit against 12, on five record formats it could have been told about. It said the xlsx was not in the branch, but the auto-commit added it.
claude_would_have_done: Same design; I would have listed each record's fields in the brief.
prompt_change: For a job over existing records, paste one sample row of each format into the brief. Tell the worker where generated files go and that the supervisor auto-commits anything left in the worktree.
scope_change: Right size: one deliverable, and the smallest overrun of the larger jobs. This supports the one-deliverable rule.

job_type: code: new status command plus listing fix
what_went_well: Found the real cause of the bad listing: name order put HP jobs first and broke early. Measured 0.326 s on 284 job folders.
waste: 100 calls against 45, reported about 99; 33 before first edit against 15, on a sandbox permission detour even though the brief warned about it, and two ordering rewrites.
claude_would_have_done: Sorted running and stalled jobs first, and dropped reviewed failures from the list. Its version keeps repeating reviewed failures for 48 hours and can push a stalled job past the 12-line limit. Both still need fixing before merge.
prompt_change: State the sort priority and when an alert stops repeating. A status tool needs its noise rules in the brief.
scope_change: Two deliverables again, listing fix and status command; it had the largest overrun against budget.

what_went_well: Tests and docs complete; two honest partial tables; it said plainly that the raw run was missing.
waste: About 49 calls before the first successful edit, about 140 total (its own count). Left unmerged for 2 days because no branch was fetched from the HP.
claude_would_have_done: Run the check on the raw run first. That run gives 1 false RIGHT (MB0928), where the worker's partial runs gave 0.
prompt_change: Put the raw run on the HP, or name the check as a merge step for the controller.
applied_in: Merged 2 Nov with the measured result at the top of the rule doc.

job_type: docs: Haiku 5.5 read 396 files in fresh sessions, 124 batches, 05:17 to 08:29 IST
what_went_well: Edits were small and cited; no edit outside a batch, no large cut; 0 reverted by the guards; ran unattended to the end without a keeper restart.
waste: 42 of 124 batches killed at the 95k limit and redone; 12 peaks passed 100k, up to 107,008, before the kill landed. Their cost is missing from the estimate.
claude_would_have_done: Known that a worktree lacks gitignored files and that the archive, .tmp and runtime are denied: about 25 false 'not in the repo' notes came from this. Also edited two bank source files and wrote one misspelt company name.
prompt_change: Prompt forbids claiming a file is gone. Lower the batch size: batches near 90,000 characters often hit the limit.
permission_change: Bank source files added to PROTECTED.
applied_in: Corrected in eb41c1e before the merge.

waste: Personal doc reading before Shivam moved it to Haiku; heredoc retries; read dsh runtime status files by script against the project deny rule, disclosed.
prompt_change: The loop prompt's 'reword a reference to a gone file' line caused the false notes; test a loop prompt against one gitignored path before an overnight run.
